objective: At the owner's request ('Continue', approving the recommendation of MUTUAL-SELECTION-20261031-001), extend mutual selection from the symmetric laws to every three-place knot, asymmetric ones included, on plain and signed cubic systems. Prove that a law whose cubic pieces pin a value (and make a pinned line an equality, and absorb spare occurrences) is as hard on cubic systems as with unbounded occurrences, hence NP-complete when it is not Schaefer-tractable; find a pinning piece for every knot that prefers a value and can fail; and state the result: the knot (not-all-equal) is the only non-affine three-place knot whose failing cubic systems can be recognised, and with KNOT-COUPLING-20261031-001 the only one with mutual selection. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-10-31: every three-place knot classified on cubic systems. Five classes (parity, Fibonacci, not-all-equal, x or (y != z), clause); only not-all-equal excludes both constants (the only knot failing on plain systems) and only it has no preferred value (cannot pin); pinning theorem (a pinning piece, an equality link and a full piece make cubic systems as hard as unbounded occurrences); one skeleton pins every pinning knot; x or (y != z) NP-complete; the clause cannot pin (Tovey). Uniqueness: assuming P != NP, not-all-equal is the only three-place knot with mutual selection. Next (awaiting the owner): value-free four-place laws on 4-regular systems (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when every three-place knot is classified (plain and signed) with proof or citation and the uniqueness theorem is proved; or when some value-preferring non-affine knot that can fail provably cannot pin (a second candidate).
title: Pinning: the knot is the only three-place law whose failures can be recognised
